article_content:
In a landmark ruling tied to one of the UK’s most harrowing migrant tragedies, 26-year-old haulier Caolan Gormley has been found guilty of conspiring to facilitate illegal immigration. The verdict comes after a two-week trial at London’s Old Bailey, where jurors learned that Gormley played a key logistical role in a smuggling ring responsible for the deaths of 39 Vietnamese nationals. Their bodies were discovered inside a refrigerated container on October 23, 2019, near Purfleet in Essex — a chilling scene that shocked the world.

Gormley, who operated a small transport business, wasn’t behind the wheel that night — that was Maurice Robinson, who opened the trailer and found the victims. But prosecutors showed he had long-standing ties to Ronan Hughes, one of the main organizers, and had been passing messages between Hughes and other drivers, including Christopher Kennedy, for multiple smuggling runs earlier in October. The victims had each paid up to £13,000 for what was sold as a ‘VIP’ passage into Europe — a promise of safety and opportunity that turned deadly.

Though police confirmed Gormley had no direct role on the night of the tragedy, his involvement in three prior operations that month painted a clear pattern. In court, Gormley expressed shock and insisted he believed he was only helping move contraband alcohol, not people. The jury didn’t buy it — after just over an hour of deliberation, they returned a unanimous guilty verdict. He remains in custody awaiting sentencing.

With this conviction, authorities say the UK’s criminal prosecution phase in the case is now complete. Yet behind the legal closure lies a deeper tragedy: dozens of lives lost because of greed, exploitation, and the dangerous gaps in international migration systems.

article_content: For nearly 20 years, Amir Saleem lived a lie — pretending to be both a brain surgeon and a qualified barrister. His elaborate deception began in 2004, when he met a 45-year-old nurse through a dating site and convinced her he was a wealthy professional living near celebrities like the Beckhams. She lent him £40,000 from her divorce settlement to buy luxury homes and cars. Over four years, their relationship produced a child, but as her suspicions grew, she ended things in 2009. Saleem later tried to sue her for custody, forcing her parents to remortgage their home to cover £25,000 in legal fees. She later described how he had shattered her life emotionally and financially, leaving her unable to work for a year due to depression. In 2012, Saleem targeted Lisa Walmsley, claiming he could help her recover £42,000 stolen by another fraudster, Selva Carmichael. He presented himself as a barrister with elite credentials, even using forged university degrees from institutions like BPP Law School and King’s College to build his credibility. He went so far as to open a fake law firm called Century Law. But during a court hearing at Manchester’s Civil Justice Centre, his facade crumbled. He made baffling legal arguments and casually bragged he was a brain surgeon who only 'dabbled in law.' When asked to spell the name of a prestigious barristers’ chambers, he misspelled 'Gray's Inn Square Barristers' Chambers.' The opposing lawyers reported him, triggering an 11-month police investigation. Police uncovered a trail of fraud: Saleem had never earned a single law degree. He’d used fake certificates to enroll in multiple university programs between 1997 and 2012. He was unemployed, lived with his parents, and was deeply in debt. In July 2023, he pleaded guilty to seven counts of deception and one count of illegally practicing law. At Manchester Crown Court, Judge David Stockdale called him a 'knowing and manipulative fraudster.' Saleem’s own lawyer admitted he existed in a 'fantasy world,' driven by self-aggrandizement. He was sentenced to four years and four months in prison. Authorities praised the investigation for exposing a man whose lies were so grandiose, they ultimately led to his undoing.

article_content: The promoter group behind Everest Food Products — famed for its iconic Everest brand of spices — has purchased a luxurious sea-view apartment in Mumbai’s exclusive Worli neighborhood for more than Rs 73.50 crore. According to an Economic Times (ET) report, the sprawling 6,130-square-foot residence is situated on the 37th floor of the Oberoi Three Sixty West tower on Dr. Annie Besant Road. The transaction translates to over Rs 1.16 lakh per square foot. The buyer, who negotiated directly with Oberoi Realty — the project’s developer — completed the registration on October 30. Additional amenities include 164 square feet of adjoining space and six dedicated car parking slots, as per official documents cited by ET. To finalize the deal, the buyer paid approximately Rs 2.41 crore in stamp duty. Notably, Oberoi Realty resold the unit within three years of acquiring it from its joint venture partner, Sahana Group. Under Indian tax regulations, stamp duty is applicable only on the profit earned from properties resold within this three-year window. Everest Food Products, founded in 1967, is India’s largest manufacturer and exporter of pure and blended spices. The Oberoi Three Sixty West complex consists of twin towers: one housing The Ritz-Carlton Hotel, the other luxury residences managed by the same brand. Oberoi Realty originally acquired over 60 units in the project from Oasis Realty — a joint venture between itself and Sahana Group — for a total investment of Rs 4,000 crore. In a separate landmark deal, the company also purchased a penthouse in the same building for Rs 230.55 crore, setting one of India’s highest-ever residential sale records. BK Goenka of the Welspun Group also bought a similarly sized penthouse in the same tower for the same price. Earlier this year, ET highlighted other major purchases by high-net-worth individuals, including billionaire investor Radhakishan Damani and his family and associates. Despite multiple attempts, neither Everest Food Products nor Oberoi Realty provided any comment at the time of reporting.

article_content: Olympic gold medalist and WNBA legend Chamique Holdsclaw has been released on $100,000 bail after being charged in connection with an alleged attack on her ex-girlfriend’s vehicle. The 35-year-old former star, who won gold with Team USA in 2000, turned herself in to Atlanta police on Thursday night following a warrant issued after the incident on Tuesday. According to authorities, Holdsclaw allegedly went to see Jennifer Lacy — a current player for the Tulsa Shock and her former partner — at a church on Atlanta’s Ponce de Leon Avenue to return personal items. When Lacy returned to her Range Rover, she says she smelled gasoline and noticed Holdsclaw following her. Lacy drove to a friend’s house, where she says Holdsclaw approached with a baseball bat and shattered the car’s rear and passenger windows. After Holdsclaw left, Lacy reported the incident. Police recovered a 9mm shell casing from inside the vehicle and believe Holdsclaw may have poured gasoline into the car earlier and fired the gun in an attempt to ignite it. No one was injured. Holdsclaw was charged with two counts of aggravated assault, possession of a firearm, two counts of criminal damage to property, and reckless conduct. She appeared in court Friday wearing a prison uniform and handcuffs, and was released under conditions that include wearing an ankle monitor, having no contact with Lacy, and appearing in court on November 30. Holdsclaw played 12 seasons in the WNBA, including a stint with the Atlanta Dream in 2009 — the same team where she played alongside Lacy. Drafted first overall in 1999 after leading the University of Tennessee Lady Vols to three straight NCAA titles, she retired in 2010 after playing for the San Antonio Silver Stars. In her 2011 autobiography, 'Breaking Through: Beating The Odds Shot After Shot,' Holdsclaw revealed her long battle with depression following the sudden death of her grandmother in 2002, which led to a suicide attempt. Today, she serves as a spokesperson for Active Minds, a nonprofit dedicated to reducing stigma around mental health among young people.

De 35-jarige voormalige ster, die goud won met Team USA in 2000, gaf zichzelf aan bij de politie in Atlanta op donderdagavond, na een arrestatiebevel dat werd uitgevaardigd na het incident op dinsdag. Volgens de autoriteiten ging Holdsclaw vermoedelijk naar Jennifer Lacy — een huidige speler van de Tulsa Shock en haar voormalige partner — op een kerk aan de Ponce de Leon Avenue in Atlanta om persoonlijke spullen terug te brengen. Toen Lacy terugkeerde naar haar Range Rover, zei ze dat ze benzinelucht rookte en Holdsclaw volgend zag. Lacy reed naar het huis van een vriend, waar ze zegt dat Holdsclaw met een honkbalknuppel naderde en de achter- en passagiersramen van de auto vernielde. article_content: At just 9.5 feet wide and 30 feet deep, 75½ Bedford Street in New York City’s Greenwich Village is the city’s narrowest home — and it has just sold for $3.25 million. Though its interior spans only 990 square feet across three stories, this historic townhouse boasts three bedrooms, two bathrooms, four wood-burning fireplaces, a secret garden, and a narrow spiral staircase winding through its length. Built around 1850 to fill a carriage entrance leading to stables behind the property, the building later served as a shoemaker’s shop and a candy factory before becoming a residence. Its fame stems not just from its size, but from its illustrious residents: Pulitzer Prize-winning poet Edna St. Vincent Millay, who wrote 'Ballad of the Harp-Weaver' here in the 1920s; actors Cary Grant and John Barrymore; anthropologist Margaret Mead; and children’s author Ann McGovern, who lived there for seven years and penned 'Mr. Skinner’s Skinny House' after being inspired by the house’s quirky charm. McGovern once recalled seeing a visitor stretch his arms wide and declare, 'Hey, I’m as big as a house!' — a moment that perfectly captures its surreal allure. In 1950, the house nearly faced demolition until a local lawyer intervened to preserve it and its neighbors. After being sold for $2.175 million in 2010, the property underwent a meticulous renovation in 2011, raising its asking price to $4.3 million before settling at $3.495 million. It finally sold for $3.25 million. Modern updates — including marble countertops, French windows, exposed beams, and a claw-foot tub opening onto a private balcony — blend seamlessly with original details, preserving its character while offering contemporary comfort. Today, it remains a popular stop on New York walking tours, celebrated as both an architectural oddity and a living piece of cultural history.

Zijn faam komt niet alleen door zijn formaat, maar ook door zijn vooraanstaande bewoners: de Pulitzer-winnende dichteres Edna St. Vincent Millay, die hier in de jaren twintig 'Ballad of the Harp-Weaver' schreef; acteurs Cary Grant en John Barrymore; antropoloog Margaret Mead; en kinderboekenschrijfster Ann McGovern, die zeven jaar hier woonde en 'Mr. Skinner’s Skinny House' schreef na geïnspireerd te zijn door de eigenaardige charme van het huis. article_content: On April 19, 2-year-old Caleigh Harrison disappeared from Long Beach in Rockport, Massachusetts, after her mother stepped away briefly to retrieve a tennis ball she’d thrown for their dog. Her 4-year-old sister later told her father she saw a man with black shorts, facial hair, and a cigarette take Caleigh. Anthony Harrison, the girl’s father, has expressed strong belief in his daughter’s account and suspects an abduction. However, Massachusetts State Police have found no physical evidence, eyewitness accounts, or surveillance footage supporting the presence of a suspect or any criminal act. Extensive search efforts—including underwater dives, drone flights, K-9 units, and ground patrols—have turned up nothing. Caleigh’s mother, Allison Hammond, says her older daughter has become emotionally withdrawn, refusing to talk about the day and showing a blank expression when shown her own drawings. A forensic child interviewer spoke with the sister, though details remain confidential. While Harrison stands by his daughter’s words as genuine and heartfelt, authorities emphasize that without corroborating evidence, the abduction theory remains speculative. No bystanders—including surfers, walkers, or nearby residents—reported seeing anything suspicious or witnessing Caleigh enter the water.

Caleigh’s moeder, Allison Hammond, zegt dat haar oudere dochter emotioneel afgesloten is geworden, weigert om over de dag te praten en een lege uitdrukking krijgt wanneer ze haar eigen tekeningen ziet. Hoewel Harrison vasthoudt aan de oprechtheid en hartelijkheid van de woorden van zijn dochter, benadrukken de autoriteiten dat zonder bevestigend bewijs de theorie van een ontvoering speculatief blijft. Geen omstanders—inclusief surfers, wandelaars of buurtbewoners—rapporteerden iets ongewoons of dat ze Caleigh het water zagen gaan.

article_content: On Friday, Egypt was hit by a series of violent explosions, adding to the country’s ongoing instability. In Cairo, at least three blasts struck key locations — one near the Ramses metro station, killing one person and wounding others; another in Heliopolis that took the life of a police officer and injured four more; and a third at a traffic checkpoint. Meanwhile, in El Tur, a city in the volatile Sinai Peninsula, two suicide attacks targeted a joint police-military checkpoint and a tour bus carrying workers, leaving one dead and nine injured. An additional attack about 50 kilometers northwest of Sharm el-Sheikh wounded three people. These incidents follow a sharp rise in militant activity in Sinai since the military ousted President Mohamed Morsy in 2013. Once Egypt’s first democratically elected president after Hosni Mubarak, Morsy was later arrested on charges including incitement to murder. His supporters continued to gather in protest across the country, defying a ban on demonstrations and the outlawing of the Muslim Brotherhood. In Helwan, Cairo, security forces dispersed the crowd, stating that protesters opened fire — a claim echoed by the Interior Ministry in a Facebook post. Elsewhere, in western Alexandria, two Morsy supporters were fatally shot during confrontations with local residents after Friday prayers, while three others were injured. Authorities responded by arresting 42 individuals linked to the pro-Morsy movement in Cairo, Giza, Fayoum, and Alexandria. The events underscore the deepening divide in Egyptian society and the government’s hardline response to dissent.

Tegelijkertijd vonden in El Tur, een stad in de kwetsbare Sinaï-schiereiland, twee zelfmoordaanslagen plaats op een gezamenlijk politie-militair controlepunt en een tourbus met werknemers aan boord, waardoor één persoon omkwam en negen gewond raakten. In Helwan, Caïro, verspreidden de veiligheidstroepen de menigte en stelden dat de demonstranten op de politie hadden geschoten — een bewering die werd bevestigd door het Binnenlands Ministerie in een Facebook-post. article_content: Shaneen Allen, a 27-year-old mother of two from Philadelphia, is facing a mandatory three-year prison sentence after being arrested in New Jersey during a routine traffic stop for carrying a legally owned handgun. Though she holds a valid concealed carry permit in Pennsylvania and voluntarily disclosed the firearm to police, New Jersey does not recognize out-of-state gun licenses. Her .380 Bersa Thunder, loaded with hollow-point bullets, violates New Jersey law—even though she purchased it only a week earlier for self-defense after her home was broken into twice. Her attorney, Evan Nappen, describes Allen as a law-abiding, hardworking single mother with no criminal record beyond minor traffic violations. He argues that her prosecution reflects an unjust application of New Jersey’s stringent gun regulations. Nappen is advocating for federal legislation requiring all states to honor each other’s concealed carry permits—a proposal he has named 'Shaneen’s Law.' While New Jersey prosecutors have denied her entry into a diversion program, legal experts acknowledge the tension between state sovereignty and national mobility. Professor Kermit Roosevelt of the University of Pennsylvania Law School affirmed that while New Jersey has the legal right to enforce its own laws, a nationwide reciprocity standard could better protect travelers and reduce unintended legal risks.

Hoewel ze een geldige vergunning voor verborgen dragen heeft in Pennsylvania en het vuurwapen vrijwillig aan de politie heeft meegedeeld, erkent New Jersey geen buitenlandse wapenlicenties. article_content: New research suggests that growing up in a loving, stimulating home plays a crucial role in shaping a child’s brain—and their future cognitive abilities. A study led by scientists from Harvard University and Boston Children’s Hospital found that children raised in institutional settings, like orphanages, have significantly less grey and white matter in their brains compared to peers raised in family environments. Grey matter, vital for memory, emotions, and speech, was notably reduced in institutionalized children, while white matter—which helps transmit signals across the brain—was closer to normal levels in those later placed in foster care. This hints at the brain’s capacity to recover, especially when intervention happens early. The team analyzed MRI scans of over 100 Romanian orphans aged 8 to 11, many of whom were moved into high-quality foster homes. Their findings, published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, point to a critical window: children placed in nurturing homes before age two showed the strongest neurological improvements. Experts say institutional care often lacks the emotional engagement and sensory stimulation needed for healthy brain wiring. With low caregiver ratios and rigid routines, these environments fail to provide the rich experiences that help children thrive. The study reinforces that early adoption or foster placement isn’t just emotionally beneficial—it’s neurologically transformative.

Een studie geleid door wetenschappers van Harvard University en Boston Children’s Hospital vond dat kinderen die opgroeiden in institutionele instellingen, zoals weeshuizen, aanzienlijk minder grijs en witte hersenweefsel hebben dan peergroepen die in familieomgevingen werden opgevoed. Grijs weefsel, essentieel voor geheugen, emoties en spraak, was duidelijk verminderd bij geïnstitutionaliseerde kinderen, terwijl witte stof—die signalen door het brein verzendt—nabij normale niveaus was bij kinderen die later in pleeggezinnen kwamen. Dit wijst op het vermogen van de hersenen om te herstellen, vooral wanneer interventie vroeg plaatsvindt. Het team analyseerde MRI-scans van meer dan 100 Roemeense wezen tussen de 8 en 11 jaar, waarvan veel werden overgeplaatst naar hoogwaardige pleeggezinnen. Hun bevindingen, gepubliceerd in de Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, wijzen op een kritische periode: kinderen die vóór de leeftijd van twee jaar in een zorgzame omgeving kwamen, toonden de sterkste neurale verbeteringen. Experten zeggen dat institutioneel onderwijs vaak ontbreekt aan emotionele betrokkenheid en zintuiglijke stimulatie die nodig zijn voor gezonde hersenontwikkeling. Met lage verzorgers-kindverhoudingen en starre routines kunnen deze omgevingen de rijke ervaringen niet bieden die kinderen helpen te gedijen. De studie bevestigt dat vroege adoptie of pleeggezinsopname niet alleen emotioneel voordelig is—het is ook neurologisch transformerend.

article_content: What a treat: guest host Billy Porter kicked off Week 8 of Dancing with the Stars with a powerful performance of 'How Will I Know'—a far more fitting start than many of the show’s past gimmicks. Before the dancing began, Porter shared his guiding principles: 'I’ll be looking for storytelling. I’ll be looking for connection. And I’ll be looking for intention.' The unspoken message? Honor Whitney Houston’s legacy with sincerity. Reality star Harry Jowsey (Too Hot to Handle), partnered with Rylee Arnold, struggled through rehearsals—his self-deprecating joke about not knowing how to dance rang true. Though Arnold’s bandaged shoulders drew attention, Jowsey looked dashing in his crushed blue velvet suit. Porter criticized him for mouthing the lyrics throughout, calling it 'distracting'—a comment many viewers found overly harsh. Score: 33/40. Her joy was palpable, and Tonioli declared, 'My daring, so sophisticated, so classy!' The performance flowed seamlessly with the music. Score: 36/40. Ariana Madix (Vanderpump Rules) owned the Paso Doble to 'Queen of the Night.' With her rising fame and entrepreneurial ventures, she seemed destined for the finale. Carrie Ann Inaba said, 'You don’t miss a moment—you attack with everything you’ve got.' Score: 39/40. Xochitl Gomez (Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness), despite a lingering ankle sprain from last week’s team dance, delivered a flawless tango to 'I Want To Dance With Somebody.' Inaba added, 'Allison danced little tiny circles around Harry.' Winner: Hannigan. Mraz faced Williams in a salsa showdown. The crowd erupted when Williams dramatically revealed his freshly shaved chest. Hough declared, 'Barry, when I grow up, I want to be like you.' Mraz knew he was out. Winner: Williams. Lawson and Gomez battled in a cha-cha. Despite Lawson’s dazzling fringe dress, Gomez’s technique was sharper, crisper, and more commanding. Alfonso Ribeiro called it 'a battle of the titans.' Inaba noted, 'One of you was just a little more competitive—it was the eye of the tiger.' Winner: Lawson. The bottom three: Williams, Mraz, and Lawson. article_content: During the final stretch of campaigning in Telangana, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi made an unannounced stop at a local restaurant in Hyderabad, where he chatted warmly with employees and diners. Dressed casually in a white polo shirt and trousers, he spent time listening and exchanging light-hearted remarks, creating a relaxed, personable atmosphere. A video shared online captured Gandhi seated with a small crowd, deeply engaged in conversation — part of his broader outreach alongside Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge. Earlier that day, Gandhi visited Ashok Nagar, meeting young people preparing for competitive exams. On his official social media account, he reflected on their struggles: 'Many believed that the creation of Telangana would open doors for them. Yet, after ten years, their dreams remain unfulfilled.' He directly challenged the BRS-led state government, stating, 'The youth of Telangana have borne the brunt of poor governance over the last decade. But their resilience and ambition are undeniable — and that’s why Congress is committed to delivering 2 lakh government jobs within our first year in power. This isn’t just a promise — it’s a guarantee.' This pledge comes against the backdrop of repeated disruptions in public sector hiring. The Telangana High Court recently annulled the Group-1 recruitment exam — the second time this year — after students raised serious concerns about exam integrity. The exam, originally scheduled for June 11 by the TSPSC, was scrapped following allegations of paper leaks and procedural violations.

article_content: It's not college students or teenagers, but middle-aged Americans who are most likely to die from drinking too much alcohol too quickly, according to a study released by the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) on Tuesday. An average of six people die each day in the United States from alcohol poisoning or dangerously high blood alcohol levels, typically caused by binge drinking, the federal study found. Three out of four of those who died were between the ages of 35 and 64 — countering the popular belief that young people are more likely than older adults to die from binge drinking. A striking finding: Middle-aged American men, not college students or teenagers, are most likely to die from binge drinking, according to the CDC study. Only 5.1 percent of the deaths occurred among drinkers aged 15 to 24, the study found. 'Contrary to conventional wisdom, there is a lot of binge drinking happening among people past college age,' said study co-author Robert Brewer. 'We were surprised by these findings.' The CDC defines binge drinking as consuming four or more drinks for women or five or more drinks for men in a single occasion. Fewer than one-third of those who died from alcohol poisoning were classified as alcoholics, the study found. Analyzing death certificate data from 2010 through 2012, researchers found that an average of 2,200 people — more than half of them white males — died from alcohol poisoning each year. State death rates ranged from a low of 5.3 deaths per million residents in Alabama to a high of 46.5 per million in Alaska. Regions with the highest death rates included the Great Plains, the West, and New England. 'Living in geographically isolated rural areas may increase the likelihood that a person with alcohol poisoning is not found before death or that timely emergency medical care is unavailable,' the researchers wrote.

Gemiddeld sterven elke dag zes mensen in de Verenigde Staten aan alcoholvergiftiging of gevaarlijk hoge bloedalcoholwaarden, meestal veroorzaakt door binge drinken, zo vond de federale studie. Drie op vier van de overledenen waren tussen de 35 en 64 jaar oud — wat de populaire overtuiging tegenspreekt dat jongeren vaker dan oudere volwassenen sterven aan binge drinken. Een opvallende bevinding: Mannelijke middenouderen, niet studenten of tieners, zijn het meest waarschijnlijk om te sterven aan binge drinken, volgens de CDC-studie. Slechts 5,1 procent van de doden kwam uit de leeftijdsgroep van 15 tot 24 jaar, zo vond de studie. 'In tegenstelling tot conventioneel denken, is er veel binge drinken onder mensen die na hun studietijd zitten,' zei mede-auteur Robert Brewer. 'We waren verrast door deze bevindingen.' De CDC definieert binge drinken als het consumeren van vier of meer drankjes voor vrouwen of vijf of meer voor mannen in één keer. Minder dan een derde van de mensen die stierven aan alcoholvergiftiging werden geclassificeerd als alcoholisten, zo vond de studie. Regio's met de hoogste sterfterates waren de Grote Eilanden, het westen en Nieuw-Engeland. article_content: Santi Cazorla stole the spotlight with a brilliant performance as Arsenal secured a surprising 2-0 victory over Premier League champions Manchester City on Sunday. His influence extended beyond goals and assists — one moment, captured on camera, became an unforgettable highlight. After delivering a precise free-kick that Olivier Giroud headed into the net for Arsenal’s second goal, Cazorla broke into an impromptu dance right where he stood. The Spanish midfielder had already opened the scoring from the penalty spot earlier in the half. The spot-kick came after Nacho Monreal was fouled by City captain Vincent Kompany in the penalty area. As the ball hit the back of the net, Cazorla’s joyful dance was caught on film — a spontaneous celebration that ended just as Monreal arrived to join in the festivities. The win delivered a crucial three points for Arsenal in their campaign.

article_content: Bubba Watson has seized control of the Masters, posting a dazzling four-under 68 on Friday to build a three-stroke lead heading into the weekend. His momentum exploded on Augusta’s notoriously tough back nine, where he sank five birdies in a row — a feat even more impressive than the four he strung together during his 2012 victory. Watson started slowly, carding even par through the front nine, but everything changed at the 12th hole. A laser-like tee shot landed just inches from the cup, sparking a run that included a miraculous putt on the 14th to seal his third straight birdie. He closed the stretch with eight-under overall before settling for a par and a bogey on the final two holes. Combined with his opening 69, Watson stands at seven-under, the outright leader. 'It’s never easy out here,' Watson said, smiling. 'The wind played tricks on me, but I guessed right on that stretch. Honestly, I wasn’t even thinking about how many I’d made — I was just focused on the next shot.' Meanwhile, the field struggled as gusts intensified and the greens turned parched. Bill Haas, who led after round one, collapsed with a disastrous four-over at Amen Corner, finishing with a 78 and tumbling to two-over. Adam Scott, the defending champ, battled through a shaky front nine, dropping three shots, but clawed back with birdies on 12, 13, and 15 to finish at three-under. He’s tied for third with Denmark’s Thomas Bjorn, Swede Jonas Blixt, and American rookie Jordan Spieth. John Senden, another Aussie, sits one shot behind at four-under after his own 68. Golf legend Fred Couples remains in touch at two-under after a steady 71. Past champions Bernhard Langer and Larry Mize made the cut comfortably at two-over, while 1988 winner Sandy Lyle barely squeaked in at four-over. Rory McIlroy and Phil Mickelson weren’t so lucky — McIlroy shot a 77 and Mickelson a 73, both missing the cut by multiple strokes. Also failing to advance: Luke Donald, Sergio Garcia, Charl Schwartzel, and young English amateur Matthew Fitzpatrick.

article_content: Paula Radcliffe, the legendary British marathoner and outspoken critic of doping in sport, has publicly condemned German journalist Hajo Seppelt for refusing to hand over a list of 150 athletes allegedly flagged for suspicious blood samples between 2006 and 2008. Despite repeated requests from World Athletics (formerly IAAF), Seppelt has withheld the document, sparking outrage from Radcliffe, who believes transparency is vital to protect clean athletes. During a recent promotional event for the Great Manchester Run, Radcliffe expressed her fury: 'It makes me so mad he won’t give it to them. The IAAF has no idea what he’s talking about — because no one’s given them the list.' Although Seppelt claimed to have shown the list to reporters at the IOC Congress in Monaco, no official IAAF letterhead was used, no blood values were disclosed, and only a single red mark identified a British athlete — with no name revealed. Seppelt insists his source is 100% trustworthy, but without independent verification, the list remains unproven. Meanwhile, his ARD documentary also alleged systemic doping in Russian athletics, claiming nearly all Russian athletes were involved in a state-backed program. The IAAF has confirmed it has never received the document and is now consulting legal counsel, planning to ask WADA to review the materials independently. The organization emphasized that reliable blood monitoring only became feasible after the introduction of the Athlete Biological Passport in 2009, casting doubt on the credibility of older data. Radcliffe, who broke the world marathon record in London in 2003, also spoke about the personal toll of being falsely accused of doping throughout her career. 'It happens all the time,' she said. 'We need systems that protect clean athletes and restore public faith in the sport.'

De IAAF heeft geen idee waar hij het over heeft — omdat niemand ze de lijst heeft gegeven.' Hoewel Seppelt beweerde de lijst te hebben getoond aan verslaggevers tijdens het IOC-congres in Monaco, werd er geen officieel IAAF-letterhead gebruikt, werden geen bloedwaarden gepubliceerd, en werd slechts één rode markering gebruikt om een Britse atleet te identificeren — zonder naam te noemen. article_content: Legia Warsaw's legal troubles this season continued on Monday, when UEFA charged the club over a fan banner criticizing its controversial elimination from the Champions League. The latest incident follows a display by Legia supporters featuring a large image of a pig superimposed on the UEFA logo, accompanied by the slogan: 'Because Football Doesn't Matter, Money Does.' The banner, surrounded by lit flares, was unveiled before Legia’s Europa League playoff victory against Aktobe of Kazakhstan last Thursday. Legia was eliminated from the Champions League third qualifying round after fielding a suspended player against Celtic FC. UEFA awarded Celtic a 3-0 win in the second leg, advancing them to the next stage. The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) denied Legia’s urgent appeal for reinstatement and will now review the club’s claim for compensation due to lost revenue. This is the third time in four seasons that UEFA has sanctioned Legia for fan misconduct. Last season, UEFA punished the club after fans displayed racist imagery during a Champions League playoff, resulting in the closure of a stadium section. Three years ago, during a Europa League match against Hapoel Tel Aviv, fans unfurled a banner reading 'Jihad Legia' in Arabic-style script across one end of the stadium.

article_content: On Christmas Eve, Gatwick Airport descended into chaos after a sudden power failure left thousands of travelers stranded for up to 12 hours without heat, food, water, or adequate restroom access. Many described the conditions as unbearable, comparing them to those in under-resourced regions. The incident—occurring just two months after a similar outage—has triggered outrage among passengers and politicians alike. Members of Parliament accused Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP), the American private equity firm that owns Gatwick, of prioritizing profits over essential infrastructure upgrades. Despite earning £127 million in pre-tax profits in the first half of the year, GIP has been criticized for failing to prepare for foreseeable weather emergencies. The Civil Aviation Authority has confirmed it is reviewing the airport’s response and may impose penalties if negligence is found. Lawmakers, including John Mann and Graham Stringer, questioned the logic of pursuing a £13 billion expansion while basic resilience measures remain inadequate. While Gatwick officials acknowledged the severity of the storm and stated that flood-prevention efforts were underway, critics pointed out that staff reportedly left their posts as passengers waited helplessly. Airlines, too, are being scrutinized for their roles in passenger care during the crisis, though regulatory responsibility ultimately rests with the airport operator. As compensation claims begin to surface, blame-shifting between the airport and carriers is already underway—but the central question remains: How could a major UK hub, generating billions in returns, be so unprepared for a holiday-season storm?

article_content: Three correctional officers at York County Prison in Pennsylvania are on unpaid leave following allegations that they orchestrated a series of abusive 'challenges' for inmates, offering food and coffee in exchange for physical suffering. The Pennsylvania State Police are investigating the officers—David Michael Whitcomb, 28; Mark Andrew Haynes, 26; and Daniel H. Graff, 37—for official oppression, with incidents reportedly occurring between January and July 2013. The probe began after surveillance footage captured Haynes grabbing inmate David Wright by the neck. Wright later described a pattern of coercion: guards forced him and others to wrestle in a storage closet, endure choking, drink gallons of milk, consume pepper foam, eat cinnamon by the spoonful, and ingest fruit with unpeeled skins—all for basic amenities like coffee and snacks. On one occasion, Graff allegedly restricted Wright’s breathing until he nearly lost consciousness; Whitcomb reportedly choked him out, and Haynes offered food if Wright could punch him in the arm. Wright referred to these incidents as the 'Retard Olympics,' a term reflecting the degrading nature of the tasks demanded. In some cases, promised rewards were never delivered. Whitcomb and Graff have publicly denied the allegations. Whitcomb told The Mercury, 'There is no physical evidence, no medical records. This is all on the word of an inmate.' Graff suggested the claims are part of a scheme to sue the prison for millions. The officers, members of the Local 776 union of Teamsters, remain suspended for three months pending investigation. York County Prison issued a statement condemning the alleged conduct: 'The actions alleged... run counter to the professional behavior county and prison management expect and require of all staff. Misconduct within any county agency is not tolerated.'

article_content: A major new survey reveals that 32% of young people in Britain have had suicidal thoughts by the time they turn 16 — a staggering figure that underscores a deepening crisis in adolescent mental health. The report, titled 'Alone with My Thoughts,' draws on responses from over 2,000 individuals aged 16 to 25 and highlights how relentless academic pressure, crippling fears of failure, and intense dissatisfaction with body image are pushing teens to the brink. Many report feeling like failures almost daily before reaching their teenage years. Despite these alarming trends, stigma continues to silence those struggling, preventing them from seeking help. Only a quarter of young people with clinically diagnosed mental health conditions receive any form of treatment, and even those who do often face cuts to services that leave them without long-term care. In response, a new initiative called MindFull.org has launched, offering free, anonymous online counseling to 11- to 17-year-olds. Backed by leading figures including clinical psychologist Professor Tanya Byron, former Labour leader Ed Miliband, and child protection expert Professor Eileen Munroe, the platform aims to meet young people where they already are — online. Advocates argue that mental health education must become a mandatory part of the national curriculum, paired with accessible school-based counseling and a nationwide shift toward early intervention. As Professor Byron notes, if teens turn to the internet for answers, we must meet them there with real support. The message is clear: just as we invest in physical fitness and nutrition, we must prioritize emotional well-being with the same urgency and resources.

Het rapport, getiteld 'Alleen met mijn gedachten', baseert zich op reacties van meer dan 2.000 personen tussen de 16 en 25 jaar en benadrukt hoe onafgebroken academische druk, vernietigende angsten voor falen en sterke ontevredenheid met het lichaam jongeren aan de rand duwen. Veel jongeren zeggen bijna dagelijks het gevoel te hebben een mislukkeling te zijn voordat ze de tienerjaren bereiken. Ondanks deze verontrustende trends blijft stigma diegenen die worstelen stil houden, waardoor ze geen hulp zoeken. Slechts een kwart van de jongeren met een klinisch gediagnosticeerde geestelijke aandoening krijgt enige vorm van behandeling, en zelfs hen wordt vaak door bezuinigingen op diensten de langetermijnbehandeling ontzegd. Als reactie is een nieuw initiatief gestart: MindFull.org, dat gratis, anonieme online counseling biedt aan jongeren van 11 tot 17 jaar. Het platform wordt ondersteund door belangrijke figuren zoals de klinische psycholoog professor Tanya Byron, voormalig Labour-leider Ed Miliband en kinderbeschermingsexpert professor Eileen Munroe, en is bedoeld om jongeren daar te bereiken waar ze al zijn — online. Voorstanders beweren dat geestelijke gezondheidseducatie verplicht moet worden gemaakt onderdeel van het nationale curriculum, samen met toegankelijk schoolgebaseerd advies en een landelijke verschuiving naar vroegtijdige interventie. Zoals professor Byron opmerkt: als tieners naar het internet kijken voor antwoorden, moeten we er ook zijn met echte ondersteuning. De boodschap is duidelijk: net zoals we investeren in lichamelijke fitheid en voeding, moeten we emotionele welzijn met dezelfde urgentie en middelen prioriteren.

article_content: Editor’s Note: CNN.com partners with CareerBuilder.com, its exclusive provider of job listings and services. Finding a career that lets you travel isn’t easy—but if you’re a recent graduate planning a gap year, a professional seeking change, or someone eager for cultural immersion, working abroad could be your perfect fit. While not every job translates easily overseas—many require language skills, certifications, or legal paperwork—some roles open the door to global adventures. Here are five options worth considering: 1. Teacher Teaching salaries in the U.S. are modest—especially in states like South Dakota, where the average was around $33,236 (per a 2003–04 American Federation of Teachers survey). But abroad? Demand for English instructors is high. Countries like South Korea, Germany, and Switzerland offer far better compensation. In South Korea, teachers earn between $25,000 and $60,000 annually. In Switzerland, salaries range from $65,000 to $80,000. Germany adds the benefit of permanent civil service status, including full social insurance. Requirements: A bachelor’s degree in education or a related field, teaching experience, and a TESL/TEFL certification. You’ll also need a work visa and permit—often arranged by your employer. 2. Chef In the U.S., the median salary for a head chef is $40,000; in hotels, it’s $43,000. Overseas, top hotels and restaurants often cover room and board, reducing living costs. Companies like Kingsbrook USA place chefs globally. In England, a Chef de Partie earned about £14,000 ($26,730 USD) annually. Sous chefs could expect $32,458–$38,186; head chefs, $38,186–$47,732. Requirements: An associate degree and at least three years of culinary experience. References, transcripts, and health records are mandatory. 3. Massage Therapist The average U.S. massage therapist earns $30,000/year. But work on a cruise ship, and you could make $33,600–$45,600—with free lodging and full health coverage. Plus, you’ll meet people from around the world and escape the limits of a typical spa setting. Requirements: A high school diploma or associate degree, plus state-certified massage therapy credentials. U.S. citizens need a passport valid for at least three months beyond their contract. Some positions require physical exams or immunizations. 4. Au Pair / Nanny In exchange for childcare and light housework, au pairs receive room, board, and a monthly stipend—offering affordable travel and deep cultural access. In the U.S., nannies earn a median of $29,500/year. In France, au pairs received €240–€250 per month (roughly $309–$322) for 33 hours of work weekly. Pay varies by country, but the real value is experiencing life abroad. Requirements: A valid passport, work visa, international driver’s license, medical insurance, and health screening. Using a reputable agency is strongly advised for safety and visa assistance. Prior childcare experience helps, though it’s not always required. 5. Caterer U.S. catering managers earned about $35,590 annually. But if you build a strong reputation, you might land gigs with international celebrities or tour with major acts. Top entertainers rely on trusted caterers to meet dietary needs—and those relationships can lead to overseas tours. Requirements: Culinary training for leads; minimal experience for support staff. To join global tours, extensive experience is essential. A passport is mandatory.

article_content: On Saturday, thousands of pro-Russian supporters gathered in Donetsk’s Lenin Square, waving Russian flags and banners featuring Che Guevara, while not a single Ukrainian flag was visible. The crowd chanted, 'Donetsk is Russian,' echoing sentiments of regional identity distinct from Kyiv. Their gathering occurred just days after a deadly clash in the same square left a 22-year-old pro-Ukrainian activist dead — a tragedy now marked only by a small floral tribute, ignored by the demonstrators who stood with their backs to it. Local journalist Denis Kazansky noted that pro-Ukrainian citizens are too afraid to demonstrate openly after the violence. Meanwhile, pro-Russian activists have established a permanent presence in the square, operating red tents where volunteers are recruited for self-defense units and petitions are signed. Attendees answered three questions: Do you support joining the Russian-led Customs Union? Yes. Should Russian be an official language? Yes. Should Ukraine join NATO? No. Vladimir Kosolapov, a regional Communist Party leader, emphasized that most locals believe Kyiv’s government lacks legitimacy. 'We need more independence,' he said. Though 48% of Donetsk’s population identifies as ethnically Russian and 46% as Ukrainian, nearly everyone speaks Russian at home and feels stronger historical ties to Moscow than to the capital. Kosolapov stressed his Ukrainian citizenship: 'I could leave for Russia, but I won’t. This is my home. My family, my parents’ land — all here.' Despite the court rejecting a local ban on the rally, citing no public safety threat, the protest disrupted traffic as demonstrators marched toward the SBU headquarters demanding the release of Pavel Gubarev, arrested in March for leading a blockade. Though minor property damage occurred, the event remained largely peaceful. With another large rally planned for Sunday in solidarity with Crimea’s referendum, officials brace for continued unrest. For many in Donetsk, the message is clear: they want the same right to self-determination — even if it means challenging Ukraine’s territorial integrity.

De menigte zong: 'Donezk is Russisch,' een uiting van regionale identiteit die afwijkt van Kiev. Hun bijeenkomst vond plaats slechts dagen na een dodelijke confrontatie op hetzelfde plein, waarbij een 22-jarige pro-Oekraïense activist omkwam — een tragedie die nu alleen nog wordt gemarkeerd door een klein bloemenoffer, dat de demonstranten negeerden die hun rug naar het offer keerden. Lokale journalist Denis Kazansky merkte op dat pro-Oekraïense burgers te bang zijn om openlijk te demonstreren na de gewelddadigheden. Tegelijkertijd hebben pro-Russische activisten een permanente aanwezigheid op het plein gevestigd, met rode tenten waar vrijwilligers worden geworven voor zelfverdedigingsseenheden en petitieformulieren worden ondertekend. De aanwezigen beantwoordden drie vragen: Steun je de lidmaatschap van de Russische douane-unie? Ja. Moet Russisch een officiële taal zijn? Ja. Moet Oekraïne lid worden van de NAVO? Nee. Vladimir Kosolapov, een regionaal leider van de Communistische Partij, benadrukte dat de meeste lokale inwoners vinden dat de regering in Kiev onwettig is. 'We hebben meer autonomie nodig,' zei hij. Hoewel 48% van de bevolking van Donezk etnisch Russisch is en 46% etnisch Oekraïens, spreekt bijna iedereen Russisch als moedertaal en voelt men sterkere historische banden met Moskou dan met de hoofdstad. Kosolapov benadrukte zijn Oekraïense nationaliteit: 'Ik kan naar Rusland vertrekken, maar ik doe het niet. Dit is mijn thuis. Mijn familie, het land van mijn ouders — alles is hier.' Ondanks dat het gerecht een lokaal verbod op de demonstratie weigerde, omdat er geen bewijs was van een bedreiging voor de openbare veiligheid, verstoordde de demonstratie het verkeer toen de betogers marcheerden naar het hoofdkwartier van de SBU om de vrijlating van Pavel Gubarev te eisen, die in maart was gearresteerd voor het leiden van een blokkade. Hoewel er enige schade aan eigendommen werd toegebracht, bleef het evenement grotendeels vreedzaam. Met een andere grote demonstratie gepland voor zondag ter ondersteuning van het referendum in Krim, staan de autoriteiten klaar voor blijvende onrust. Voor veel mensen in Donezk is het bericht duidelijk: ze willen hetzelfde recht op zelfbeschikking — zelfs als dat betekent dat ze de territoriale integriteit van Oekraïne uitdagen.

article_content: Brazilian football legend Pelé is under fire after being quoted as suggesting that Robinho and Ronaldo used recreational drugs at a private party in São Paulo. Robinho, the former Manchester City forward, responded with deep disappointment, stating the claims are hurtful and unsubstantiated. His legal team has demanded a public retraction, warning that failure to do so may result in legal proceedings. The remarks reportedly emerged during testimony concerning Pelé’s son, Edinho, who has openly admitted to a history of cocaine addiction. Robinho’s official website clarified that while the player does not believe Pelé intended harm, the damage caused by the statements — particularly if amplified by sensationalist reporting — is unacceptable. The Brazilian radio station Jovem Pan reported Pelé as saying, 'It’s unfair to paint all of football with the brush of drug use based on isolated cases like Robinho and Ronaldo.' Robinho’s representatives urged Pelé to reconsider his stance, noting that the legendary figure’s voice carries immense weight and should reflect responsibility, not rumor.

De opmerkingen zouden zijn gedaan tijdens een getuigenis in verband met de zoon van Pelé, Edinho, die openlijk toegeeft een geschiedenis van cocaïneverslaving te hebben. article_content: Nine-year-old Kamryn Renfro shaved her head to stand beside her best friend, Delaney Clements, who lost her hair during chemotherapy for neuroblastoma, a rare childhood cancer. Kamryn wanted Delaney to know she wasn’t alone. But when Kamryn returned to Caprock Academy in Grand Junction, Colorado, school officials told her she couldn’t re-enter the classroom — her shaved head violated the dress code, which prohibits girls from shaving their heads. Kamryn felt punished. 'I was pretty sad that they didn't let me go to school,' she told the Today Show. 'I was feeling that I was punished.' Delaney, who had endured four relapses and was preparing for another round of chemotherapy, said Kamryn’s gesture meant everything. 'I was so happy that I would have somebody there for me,' she said. Kamryn’s mother, Jamie Renfro, notified the school of her daughter’s new look via email — and received a response demanding she wear a wig or wait for her hair to grow back. The school board, led by chairwoman Catherine Norton, defended the policy as necessary to maintain a 'uniform, non-distracting environment' and stated exceptions were limited. But the community reacted swiftly. After Jamie posted about the incident on Facebook, protests erupted, and the story went viral nationwide. Within days, Caprock Academy’s board held an emergency meeting and voted 3-1 to allow Kamryn back. Only board member Bill Newcomer opposed the decision, telling NBC: 'We’ve succumbed to making decisions based on emotion, not logic.' Kamryn returned to school to cheers from classmates. 'They just thought I was brave to shave my head for cancer,' she said. Her mother added, 'Proud is an understatement.' Delaney’s mother, Wendy Campbell, praised Kamryn’s courage: 'For a little girl to make such a brave choice — that builds character.' The girls’ friendship, forged in a gymnastics class, now stands as a powerful symbol of compassion — and a reminder that sometimes, kindness breaks rules for the right reason.

Maar toen Kamryn terugkeerde naar Caprock Academy in Grand Junction, Colorado, vertelden schoolfunctionarissen haar dat ze niet terug kon komen naar de klas — haar geschoren hoofd verstond de kleedcode, die meisjes verbiedt hun hoofd te schoren. Delaney, die vier recidieven had doorstaan en op het punt stond een nieuwe ronde chemotherapie te beginnen, zei dat Kamryns gebaar alles betekende. 'Ik was zo blij dat er iemand voor me was,' zei ze. Kamryns moeder, Jamie Renfro, informeerde de school via e-mail over de nieuwe uitstraling van haar dochter — en ontving een reactie waarin werd gevraagd dat ze een pruik droeg of wachtte tot haar haar weer groeide. Het schoolbestuur, geleid door voorzitter Catherine Norton, verdedigde het beleid als noodzakelijk om een 'eenparige, niet-afleidende omgeving' te behouden en stelde dat uitzonderingen beperkt waren. Maar de gemeenschap reageerde snel. Na het posten van het incident op Facebook door Jamie, braken protesten uit en ging het verhaal wereldwijd viral. Binnen enkele dagen hield het schoolbestuur van Caprock Academy een spoedvergadering en stemde met 3 tegen 1 voor Kamryns terugkeer. Alleen bestuurslid Bill Newcomer was tegen, en vertelde NBC: 'We zijn toegegeven aan het maken van beslissingen op basis van emotie, niet logica.' Kamryn keerde terug naar school onder applaus van haar klasgenoten. 'Ze vonden het gewoon dapper van me om mijn haar af te scheren voor kanker,' zei ze. Haar moeder voegde toe: 'Trots is een onderschatting.' Delaney’s moeder, Wendy Campbell, loofde Kamryns moed: 'Voor een klein meisje om zo'n dappere keuze te maken — dat bouwt karakter op.' De vriendschap tussen de meisjes, ontstaan in een turnles, staat nu als een krachtig symbool van compassie — en een herinnering dat liefde soms regels breekt voor het juiste moment.

article_content: A U.S. Black Hawk helicopter crashed in southern Afghanistan on Thursday, with all four crew members — American service members — believed to have perished, according to a U.S. military source. While heavy weather conditions were present at the time, officials stressed that enemy involvement hasn’t been excluded. Ground troops stationed at a nearby combat outpost reportedly witnessed the crash firsthand. Another helicopter operating in the vicinity escaped unscathed. Helicopter losses in Afghanistan are tragically common: some result from hostile attacks, while others stem from mechanical failures or environmental hazards. The most devastating single loss for American forces since the war began in 2001 occurred last August, when a Chinook helicopter was shot down, killing 30 U.S. troops and seven Afghan soldiers. The Taliban claimed they used a rocket-propelled grenade to bring it down. More recently, a separate crash in Kabul last month claimed 12 lives, though Capt. David Yaryar of ISAF confirmed no insurgent activity had been detected in the area at the time.

Hoewel er zware weersomstandigheden heersten, benadrukten officieren dat vijandelijke betrokkenheid niet is uitgesloten. Grondtroepen op een nabijgelegen gevechtspost hadden de crash rechtstreeks gezien. Een andere helikopter in de buurt kwam ongedeerd weg. Helikopterverliezen in Afghanistan zijn triest gebruikelijk: sommige zijn het gevolg van vijandelijke aanvallen, anderen van technische problemen of omstandigheden. Het meest fatale enkelvoudige verlies voor Amerikaanse troepen sinds de oorlog begon in 2001 vond afgelopen augustus plaats, toen een Chinook-helikopter werd neergeschoten, waardoor 30 Amerikaanse soldaten en zeven Afghaanse soldaten omkwamen. De Taliban beweerden dat ze een raketwerper gebruikten om hem neer te halen. Meer recentelijk kostte een aparte crash in Kabul afgelopen maand 12 levens, hoewel kapitein David Yaryar van ISAF bevestigde dat er geen insurgente activiteit was vastgesteld in het gebied op dat moment.

article_content: Aubrey 'Lee' Price, a 47-year-old former banker and minister from south Georgia, was captured Tuesday after 18 months on the run, authorities confirmed. The FBI announced his arrest but did not disclose details of his apprehension or his activities since June 2012. According to Glynn County Sheriff’s Office records, Price was booked on a charge of providing false information — including a false name, address, or birth date — to law enforcement and is being held for federal marshals. His capture concludes a nationwide manhunt that began in Ailey, Georgia — a small town of roughly 430 residents — and extended across Florida, Latin America, and international waters. In late 2010, Price was hailed by local leaders after acquiring control of the struggling Montgomery Bank & Trust. Prosecutors allege, however, that he never intended to invest the bank’s capital. Instead, he created a sham New York-based clearing firm to disguise fraudulent wire transfers and submitted forged documents to convince bank officials he had purchased U.S. Treasury securities. A July 2012 federal complaint stated that Price and associates raised approximately $40 million from around 115 investors, primarily in Georgia and Florida, starting in 2009. He diverted the funds into personal accounts and concealed the theft by falsely claiming $17 million had been deposited with a New York financial firm. Before vanishing in June 2012, Price reportedly told friends he had lost a large sum in trading and planned to end his life by jumping from a ferry off Florida’s coast. Yet he was sighted alive in Key West that same month. A U.S. Coast Guard search for his body turned up nothing, prompting authorities to suspect he had fled the country. Price owned real estate in Venezuela and Guatemala and possessed a 17-foot boat. The FBI offered up to $20,000 for information leading to his arrest — though it remains unclear whether the reward will be paid or how he was ultimately detained. A federal grand jury in New York indicted him earlier this year on charges of wire fraud and securities fraud. Conviction could result in up to 30 years for wire fraud and 25 years for securities fraud. Montgomery Bank & Trust, which had operated for nearly nine decades, was shuttered by Georgia regulators in summer 2012, with the FDIC appointed as receiver. Price’s family has remained silent since the charges surfaced, and it is unknown whether he has secured legal counsel following his detention.

Zijn arrestatie beëindigt een landelijke zoektocht die begon in Ailey, Georgia — een klein dorp met ongeveer 430 inwoners — en zich uitstrekte over Florida, Latijns-Amerika en internationale wateren. Eind 2010 werd Price gevierd door lokale leiders nadat hij controle kreeg over de moeilijkheden ondervindende Montgomery Bank & Trust. De aanklagers beweren echter dat hij nooit van plan was het kapitaal van de bank te investeren. Een federale klacht van juli 2012 stelde dat Price en medeplichtigen ongeveer 40 miljoen dollar hebben ingezameld van ongeveer 115 investeerders, voornamelijk in Georgia en Florida, beginnend in 2009. Toch werd hij levend gezien in Key West diezelfde maand. Een veroordeling kan leiden tot maximaal 30 jaar gevangenisstraf voor elektronische fraude en 25 jaar voor waardepapierenfraude. De Montgomery Bank & Trust, die bijna negentig jaar actief was geweest, werd in de zomer van 2012 gesloten door de staat Georgia, met de Amerikaanse Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) als ontvanger. De familie van Price is stil gebleven sinds de aanklachten bekend werden, en het is onbekend of hij juridische hulp heeft gekregen na zijn detentie.

article_content: A shop owner has described the hilarious moment thieves fled empty-handed when an employee hauled two stolen sofas out of their getaway van—after they forgot to close the doors. Dramatic CCTV footage from a furniture showroom shows a pair of men brazenly loading two brown £400 settees into a white Transit van in broad daylight. Seconds before the intruders sped off, brave store manager Justin Hallett, 37, leapt through the open back doors and reclaimed the sofas. Store owner Mark Kypta, 42, said the footage looked like 'something out of a Benny Hill film.' He added: 'We couldn’t believe their audacity—coming around the back of the store during our busiest time and brazenly loading our sofas into the van. Our prices aren’t high, so they must have been desperate.' 'Luckily, Justin—without thinking of his own safety—ran out, jumped into the back of the van, and got the sofas back. I think he’s in line for a Christmas bonus. He was incredibly brave.' 'The whole thing feels like it should have a Benny Hill soundtrack. It’s bizarre—but on a serious note, we want these guys caught. We don’t want other businesses targeted.' The 60-second clip shows two of the three-man gang jumping out of a white van with its license plate obscured. One entered the store while the other opened the van’s rear doors, then followed him inside. Moments later, both emerged carrying a large brown leather sofa, which they loaded into the van. They returned for a second three-seater before attempting to flee—with Mr. Hallett in hot pursuit. The incident occurred at the Sofa King furniture superstore near Northampton at 11:45 a.m. on Saturday. Mr. Hallett dragged both sofas back into the parking lot, undeterred by danger. The thieves sped away without them. Mark Kypta said: 'The barefaced cheek of these guys was crazy—and it could have turned nasty. Luckily, nobody was hurt, and we kept our stock. But it could have been a very different outcome.'

article_content: Rene Umberger, a 53-year-old environmental diver from Kona, Hawaii, is demanding attempted murder charges after being attacked underwater last Thursday. The incident, captured on video, shows another diver swimming toward her at a distance and violently pulling out her oxygen regulator. Umberger managed to reattach the line within 30 seconds but feared a second assault. 'I thought he was coming back for another attack,' she told Hawaii News Now. 'I got on the boat and screamed — someone just tried to kill me underwater.' With over 10,000 dives under her belt, Umberger credits her survival to experience. 'An inexperienced diver would panic — either from the sudden loss of air or fear of drowning — and surge toward the surface. That often leads to fatal decompression sickness, known as 'the bends',' she explained. Rapid ascents cause nitrogen bubbles to form in the bloodstream, risking joint pain, paralysis, or brain damage. The attacker, whose identity remains undisclosed due to lack of formal charges, was reportedly accompanied by another diver. Umberger suspects both men were commercial reef fishermen targeting fish for the aquarium trade — a practice she says is decimating fragile coral ecosystems. 'Hawaii’s reefs are being emptied by unchecked commercial harvesting,' she said. While reef fishing is legal in Hawaii under regulated permits, it is unclear whether the men violated any rules. Umberger insists she will pursue legal action. Charges have not yet been filed. 'Never in a million years did I think someone would do this — especially from so far away,' she added. 'There was no provocation. We weren’t even close.'

article_content: Robert Downey Jr. has reclaimed the title of Hollywood’s top earner, according to Forbes, pulling in an estimated $75 million between June 2013 and June 2014 — matching his earnings from the previous year. His success is closely tied to his iconic portrayal of Tony Stark/Iron Man, a role that has anchored three solo films and the record-breaking 2012 hit The Avengers. With Avengers: Age of Ultron set for release in 2015, Forbes notes that Marvel’s future in these franchises would be nearly impossible to sustain without him. Coming in second is Dwayne 'The Rock' Johnson, who earned $52 million after starring in five films during the same period. Bradley Cooper follows in third with $46 million, a figure that complements his recent critical acclaim and Oscar nominations. Rounding out the top five are Leonardo DiCaprio with $39 million and Chris Hemsworth, who portrayed Thor and brought in approximately $37 million. Forbes gathers its figures by consulting producers, agents, and legal teams to estimate gross income before taxes, management fees, or other deductions. For the complete ranking, readers are directed to Forbes.com.

article_content:
In a heartbreaking turn of events, 20-year-old Kayla Henriques was sentenced to 15 years in prison for the 2011 fatal stabbing of her brother’s girlfriend, Kamisha Richards, 22. What began as a simple $20 loan — meant to help Henriques buy essentials for her one-year-old son — spiraled into a violent tragedy after a bitter dispute over money spilled into both online and physical spaces. When Henriques used the cash for something else, Richards confronted her, retaliating by emptying the baby’s milk from the fridge. The tension flared further on Facebook, where messages grew hostile, including a chilling exchange: Richards wrote, 'This is the last time you’ll con me,' to which Henriques replied, 'We’ll see.'

The confrontation moved offline later that evening at Henriques’ grandmother’s home in East New York. During a heated argument — even as they continued texting inside the same room — Henriques grabbed a knife and Richards seized scissors. In the chaos, Henriques stabbed Richards once. Witnesses described Richards as calm after being injured, and a relative rushed to her side, applying pressure and calling for help. She was pronounced dead at Brookdale University Hospital.

Richards, a recent graduate of John Jay College of Criminal Justice and a security guard for JPMorgan Chase, had dreams of attending law school and was preparing a birthday party for baby Alex. Henriques, overwhelmed with guilt, publicly apologized on Facebook, writing, 'I can’t believe this happened... RIP Kamisha.' She accepted a plea deal that reduced the charge from murder to manslaughter, avoiding a possible 25-years-to-life sentence. Sentencing was finalized on August 21, marking the end of a case that began with a small debt — and ended with a life lost.

Toen Henriques het geld gebruikte voor iets anders, confronteerde Richards haar en nam wraak door de melk van de baby uit de koelkast te leegmaken. De spanning steeg verder op via Facebook, waar berichten vijandig werden, inclusief een griezelige uitwisseling: Richards schreef: 'Dit is de laatste keer dat je me bedriegt,' waarna Henriques antwoordde: 'We zullen zien.'

De confrontatie verplaatste zich later die avond naar het huis van Henriques’ grootmoeder in East New York. Tijdens een heftig geschil — terwijl ze nog steeds tekstberichten uitleverden in dezelfde kamer — greep Henriques een mes en Richards een schaar. In de chaos stak Henriques Richards eenmaal. Getuigen beschreven Richards als kalm na de verwonding, en een familielid haastte zich naar haar toe, druk uitoefende op de wond en de hulpdiensten belde. Richards, een recente afgestudeerde van John Jay College of Criminal Justice en beveiliger bij JPMorgan Chase, had dromen om rechtsschool te gaan en was bezig met het plannen van een verjaardagsfeestje voor baby Alex. Ze accepteerde een pleidooi-overeenkomst die de aanklacht verlaagde van moord naar doodslag, en zo een mogelijke straf van 25 jaar tot leven voorkwam. article_content: In eastern Uganda, a devastating landslide triggered by days of heavy rain has buried entire communities near Mount Elgon, leaving hundreds feared dead. Authorities estimate around 300 people are still missing—including 100 students—after the wall of mud swept through villages like Nametsi, Namakansa, and Kubewo, which have been virtually erased from the map. So far, rescuers have recovered at least 87 bodies, though officials have reduced earlier estimates of 106 fatalities after determining some remains were fragments too incomplete to count as full individuals. Rescue teams, including Uganda’s military and local residents armed with shovels, hoes, and even bare hands, are struggling to reach survivors amid treacherous slopes and relentless rainfall. Heavy machinery cannot be deployed, officials warn, as the unstable ground could trigger further slides. The nearest accessible roads are miles away, forcing evacuees to walk up to 10 kilometers to temporary camps. The Ugandan Red Cross, United Nations, and World Food Programme are delivering food, clean water, blankets, and setting up mobile clinics to support thousands displaced by the disaster. President Yoweri Museveni visited the site, presiding over a solemn funeral for victims attended by only a handful due to ongoing safety risks. He has since ordered the evacuation of nearly 4,000 residents from high-risk zones to safer, flatter areas. With no survivors found in recent days, rescuers have shifted focus entirely to recovery. Flooding linked to the landslide has also damaged roads and washed out bridges across at least seven districts, compounding the humanitarian crisis.
translated_content: In het oosten van Oeganda heeft een verwoestende aardverschuiving, uitgelokt door dagenlang zware regen, hele gemeenschappen rond Mount Elgon begraven, waarbij honderden mensen vermist worden en waarschijnlijk dood zijn. Autoriteiten schatten dat ongeveer 300 mensen nog steeds vermist zijn — waaronder 100 studenten — nadat een muur modder dorpen als Nametsi, Namakansa en Kubewo heeft weggespoeld, die vrijwel van de kaart zijn gevaagd. Tot nu toe hebben reddingsploegen minstens 87 lijken gevonden, hoewel officiële cijfers zijn teruggebracht van 106 naar lager, omdat sommige resten te onvolledig werden geacht om als volledige personen te worden geteld. Reddingsploegen, waaronder het Oegandese leger en lokale bewoners met schoppen, hooien en zelfs bloote handen, worstelen met het bereiken van overlevenden in het gevaarlijke terrein en onder aanhoudende regenval. Zware machines kunnen niet worden ingezet, waarschuwen autoriteiten, omdat het onstabiele grondgesteente verdere aardverschuivingen zou kunnen veroorzaken. De dichtstbijzijnde toegankelijke wegen liggen kilometers verder, waardoor ontheemden tot wel 10 kilometer moeten lopen naar tijdelijke kampen. Het Oegandese Rode Kruis, de Verenigde Naties en het Wereldvoedselprogramma leveren voedsel, schoon water, dekens en richten mobiele klinieken in om duizenden ontheemden te ondersteunen. President Yoweri Museveni bezocht de plek en leidde een beklomme begrafenis voor de slachtoffers, waar slechts een handvol aanwezig was vanwege de aanhoudende veiligheidsrisico’s. Hij heeft sindsdien de evacuatie van bijna 4.000 bewoners uit risicogebieden naar veiliger, vlakkere gebieden bevolen. Met geen enkele overlevende de laatste dagen gevonden, hebben reddingsploegen hun focus volledig verschoven naar het bergen van lijken. Vloedgolven in verband met de aardverschuiving hebben ook wegen beschadigd en bruggen weggespoeld in ten minste zeven districten, wat de humanitaire crisis verergert.

article_content: Alan Taylor, a 51-year-old nurse, has been sentenced to 12 and a half years in prison for sexually abusing two vulnerable female patients on a psychiatric ward in Hertfordshire between 2005 and 2007. Taylor exploited his position of trust, committing multiple acts of sexual abuse—including sexual intercourse, groping, and forcing victims to touch him—in private areas such as patient rooms, hospital cupboards, nearby woodland, and even his own bedroom on hospital grounds. He repeatedly covered observation windows to conceal his crimes during night shifts. At St Albans Crown Court, he was convicted on five counts of sexual activity with a person with a mental disorder. In addition to his prison term, Taylor has been permanently barred from working as a carer by the Nursing and Midwifery Council and must register as a sex offender for life. Judge Stephen Warner condemned Taylor for ‘systematically abusing his position of trust’ to exploit some of society’s most vulnerable individuals. Detective Constable Kelly Adams described him as ‘despicable’ and highlighted the emotional toll on both victims and investigators. The Hertfordshire Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust called his actions ‘completely unacceptable,’ while the Crown Prosecution Service praised the victims’ extraordinary courage in testifying years after the trauma. Their resilience, prosecutors said, was vital in bringing justice to light.

Taylor misbruikte zijn positie van vertrouwen door meerdere seksuele handelingen te plegen — waaronder seksuele penetratie, aaien en het dwingen van slachtoffers om hem aan te raken — in privéruimtes zoals patiëntenkamers, kasten in het ziekenhuis, nabijgelegen bosjes en zelfs zijn eigen slaapkamer op het ziekenhuisterrein. Hij bedekte herhaaldelijk de kijkvensters om zijn misdaden tijdens zijn nachtdienst te verbergen. Bij de rechtbank van St Albans werd hij schuldig bevonden aan vijf tellingen van seksuele activiteit met een persoon met een mentale stoornis. Naast zijn gevangenisstraf is Taylor voor altijd verboden om als zorgverlener te werken door de Nursing and Midwifery Council en moet hij zich voor zijn hele leven registreren als seksoffender. Rechter Stephen Warner veroordeelde Taylor voor het ‘systematisch misbruiken van zijn positie van vertrouwen’ om de meest kwetsbare leden van de samenleving te exploiteren. Detaché-constable Kelly Adams beschreef hem als ‘verschrikkelijk’ en benadrukte de emotionele belasting voor zowel slachtoffers als onderzoekers. De Hertfordshire Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust noemde zijn daden ‘volledig onaanvaardbaar’, terwijl de Openbare Aanklager de buitengewone moed van de slachtoffers prijste om jaren na het trauma te getuigen. Hun vastberadenheid, zeiden de aanklagers, was essentieel voor het tot stand brengen van gerechtigheid.

article_content: Losing weight without dieting or exercise sounds like a dream—but now, a scientist claims a wearable 'ice jacket' might make it possible. Developed by Professor Wayne Hayes of the University of California and a visiting scientist at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory, the Cold Shoulder Jacket is designed to burn up to 500 calories per day—roughly the energy in a Big Mac, two Snickers bars, or four slices of bacon. The jacket contains frozen gel packs that cool the shoulders and upper back—the areas where the body stores most of its brown adipose tissue, or 'brown fat.' Unlike white fat, which stores energy, brown fat burns calories to generate heat. By exposing these regions to mild cold, the jacket prompts the body to increase its metabolic activity to maintain core temperature. Crucially, the design avoids discomfort: the gel packs are positioned where nerve endings are sparse, so users don’t shiver or feel painfully cold—even though the jacket is taken directly from the freezer and worn over a shirt. Professor Hayes says users typically adapt quickly, often forgetting they’re wearing it. To be effective, the jacket must be worn while at rest in a comfortably warm environment—not during exercise or in hot weather. In those cases, the cooling effect simply provides relief rather than triggering calorie burn. Hayes conducted a small clinical trial with eight participants, finding that wearing the jacket for about an hour, twice daily, increased daily calorie expenditure by approximately 500 calories—equal to roughly one pound of fat per week (since 3,500 calories ≈ 1 lb of fat). However, he stresses this is not a free pass to indulge. 'You can easily cancel out the benefit by eating an extra 500 calories,' he warns. The jacket is intended as a supportive tool for those already reducing calorie intake, not a replacement for healthy habits. Hayes defends the innovation by comparing it to other extreme weight-loss methods: 'Starving yourself? Wearing a corset? Injecting chemicals? Freezing fat cells? Compared to those, this is pretty tame.' Priced at $160 and available in sizes XS to XXXL, the Cold Shoulder Jacket is marketed as a practical, non-surgical option for weight management—especially useful for postpartum recovery or holiday binges. While mild cold exposure is generally safe for healthy individuals, those with circulatory or neurological conditions should consult a physician before use. For more details, visit the official Cold Shoulder website.
translated_content: Gewicht verliezen zonder te diëten of te sporten klinkt als een droom—maar nu beweert een wetenschapper dat een draagbare 'ijsjasje' het mogelijk zou kunnen maken. Ontwikkeld door professor Wayne Hayes van de Universiteit van Californië en een bezoekende wetenschapper bij NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory, is het Cold Shoulder-jasje ontworpen om tot wel 500 calorieën per dag te verbranden—ongeveer de energie in een Big Mac, twee Snickers of vier plakken spek. Het jasje bevat bevroren gelzakjes die de schouders en bovenrug koelen—de gebieden waar het lichaam het meeste bruine vetweefsel, of 'bruin vet', opslaat. Anders dan wit vet, dat energie opslaat, verbrandt bruin vet calorieën om warmte te genereren. Door deze gebieden bloot te stellen aan milde kou, wordt het lichaam aangemoedigd om zijn metabolisme te verhogen om de kerntemperatuur te behouden. Belangrijk is dat het ontwerp ongemak voorkomt: de gelzakjes zijn geplaatst waar zenuwuiteinden schaars zijn, dus gebruikers trillen niet of voelen geen pijnlijke kou—zelfs als het jasje direct uit de vriezer komt en over een shirt wordt gedragen. Professor Hayes zegt dat gebruikers zich snel aanpassen en vaak vergeten dat ze het dragen. Om effectief te zijn, moet het jasje worden gedragen terwijl je in een comfortabel warme omgeving rust—niet tijdens sporten of in warm weer. In die gevallen biedt de koeling gewoon verkoeling, maar activeert het geen calorieverbranding. Hayes voerde een kleine klinische studie uit met acht deelnemers en vond dat het dragen van het jasje ongeveer een uur lang, tweemaal daags, het dagelijkse calorieverbruik met ongeveer 500 calorieën verhoogde—gelijk aan ongeveer één pond vet per week (aangezien 3.500 calorieën ≈ 1 pond vet). Hij benadrukt echter dat dit geen vrije kaart is om te genieten. 'Je kunt het voordeel gemakkelijk tenietdoen door 500 extra calorieën te eten,' waarschuwt hij. Het jasje is bedoeld als ondersteunend hulpmiddel voor mensen die al hun calorieëntoevoer verminderen, niet als vervanging voor gezonde gewoonten. Hayes verdedigt de innovatie door het te vergelijken met andere extreme gewichtsverliesmethoden: 'Jezelf laten verhongeren? Een korset dragen? Chemische injecties? Vetcellen bevriezen? In vergelijking daarmee is dit vrij bescheiden.' Prijs: $160 en beschikbaar in maten XS tot XXXL. Het Cold Shoulder-jasje wordt gemarket als een praktische, niet-chirurgische optie voor gewichtsbeheersing—vooral nuttig voor postpartum-herstel of feestdagen. Hoewel milde koublootstelling over het algemeen veilig is voor gezonde personen, moeten mensen met circulatoire of neurologische aandoeningen eerst een arts raadplegen. Meer informatie op de officiële Cold Shoulder-website.

article_content: CNN — Sheila Ranea Crabtree of Pataskala, Ohio, has legally changed her first name to Sexy Ranea Crabtree. The 41-year-old former photographer completed the change at the Licking County courthouse on Tuesday. She has gone by her middle name since high school and says her birth name, Sheila, was chosen by her father — someone she has seen only a few times in her life. She emphasizes that the decision was not an act of rebellion. 'I’ve always hated Sheila,' she told CNN. 'Now I am free from that name.' She selected 'Sexy' over alternatives like 'Sparkle' and 'Sinder' because it reflects her personality. Her husband supports the change, and when asked how her mother will address her, she replied without hesitation: 'Sexy Ranea.'
